beats: [d:intrigue][sfx:boom][act:hushed, wonder]About seven thousand years ago, in the Egyptian Sahara, cattle herders set up a small circle of ^stones.
[d:tension][act:the question, leaning in][tune:rise]Was it the world's first ^observatory? [act:explaining, plain]A place built to watch the ^sky?

[d:calm][act:plain, orienting]The place is called Nabta ^Playa. [act:steady, factual]It lies about a hundred kilometres west of Abu ^Simbel, in the far south of ^Egypt. [p:0.93][act:explaining, a simple picture]A playa is a dry lake bed: a flat hollow that only holds water after ^rain. [act:steady, vivid]Back then, summer rains filled it into a seasonal ^lake, and herders came with their ^cattle.

[d:build][act:building, precise]The circle is small: only about four metres ^across. [act:light, a small smile]You could cross it in five ^strides. [act:pointing them out]Around its edge stand four pairs of upright ^stones, like little ^gateposts. [p:0.93][act:the claim, intrigued]Look through two of the gaps, and your line of sight runs north to ^south. [act:the second one, wonder]And a second line points to where the sun rises at ^midsummer, on the longest day of the ^year.

[d:build][act:the reveal, strong]It's some seven thousand years ^old, perhaps older. [p:0.93][act:context, wonder]That's at least eighteen centuries before the first phase of ^Stonehenge. [act:a picture of time, unhurried]Eighteen centuries: about as long as the time that separates ^us from the Roman ^Empire.

[d:build][go:4|0][act:vivid]Nearby, cattle were buried in clay-lined ^chambers. [p:0.93][act:vivid, impressed]And stones nearly three metres ^tall, taller than the ceiling of a room, were dragged across the sand into ^lines.

[d:reveal][act:fair, the challenger's case]Some go much ^further. [act:presenting it, fair]They see lines to bright ^stars, even a map of the constellation ^Orion, laid out in stone. [p:0.93][act:explaining, clear]But the stars shift slowly over the centuries, so a line to a star only works at one ^time. [p:0.9][act:the reply, precise]And those star dates fall about fifteen hundred years ^before the stones were set up. [act:fair, careful]Some stones may also have ^moved since.
[d:build][act:plain, a small smile][tune:fall]Even the excavators say its nickname, the calendar circle, may be the wrong ^name.

[d:verdict][p:0.95][act:weighing it, even][tune:rise]The world's first ^observatory? [act:the verdict, measured][tune:fall]*Mixed ^record@noun*. [act:fair]A real ritual landscape, probably watching the ^sun. [act:fair, explaining]The north line and the midsummer sunrise hold up ^well.
[d:tension][p:0.93][act:the last word, warm][tune:fall]The star maps are a ^stretch.
